title: Surprise me
description: Discover unexpected opportunities through seeded exploration.
questions: Select a specific person and recurring situation, then research before proposing a product.
Search outside familiar AI and productivity categories; retain a record of rejected directions.
Randomness chooses search directions, never supplies evidence or customer numbers.

title: Improve an existing app
description: Investigate the decisions around one application.
questions: Describe the decision served and the steps immediately before and after.
Find actual complaints, feature requests, exports, and companion-tool mentions.
Separate improvement to the seed app from a standalone product; neither classification automatically kills it.

title: Combine existing apps
questions: Map the same person and task across the reference apps.
Identify repeated entry, lost context, conflicting records, and unfinished actions.
Explain why the joined workflow is more valuable than integration overhead; remove any unnecessary component.

title: Build from a repository
description: Find applications for a specific technical capability.
questions: Inspect README, manifests and selected implementation; pin revision and exact source paths.
Separate advertised functionality from source-inspected and runtime-tested capabilities.
Find people already performing the enabled task and identify missing product infrastructure.

title: Find an underserved buyer
description: Investigate structural exclusion by pricing and delivery.
questions: Record incumbent price, packaging mechanism, minimum commitment, source and date.
Name the excluded buyer and their existing workaround; test whether exclusion reflects bad economics.
Explain the depth or workflow difference beyond discounting; incumbent responses are hypotheses.

title: Remove manual work
description: Find a repetitive tax worth removing or assisting.
questions: Measure task, frequency, time, existing costs, and the source of each number.
Separate tax, craft, ritual and coordination; consider assistive tools before rejecting craft wholesale.
Identify embedded judgment, exception handling, and what is lost through automation; annual work can support transaction pricing.

title: Connect data into a decision
description: Find a useful join that changes a decision.
questions: Identify the decision and the variables that can change its answer.
Name at least two sources and assess keys, coverage, freshness, access, uncertainty and use rights.
Specify the smallest useful dataset, a fallback and a test of actual decision improvement.

title: Exploit a recent change
description: Find newly viable offers and migration needs.
questions: Verify the dated change and identify affected users; never invent a retirement date.
Describe the former constraint and how the change alters a workflow or economics.
Estimate the window as a scenario, not a fact; identify what closes it and how customers can be reached.

title: Transfer across industries
description: Move a proven mechanism to a new context.
questions: Extract the mechanism behind a reference, rather than copying its surface.
Find another setting with comparable incentives and identify where the analogy breaks.
Research local workflow, buyer authority, distribution and constraints independently.

title: Compose from my capabilities
description: Search catalogs for useful combinations without confusing supply with demand.
questions: Search Maliky for available assets and Every Awesome Repo for external leads; preserve ownership distinctions.
Identify complementary capabilities, compatibility gaps, licensing and maintenance costs.
Find independent buyer evidence and compare a minimal product against the impressive but unnecessary bundle.
